thread:
Maya (VP Eng): Thanks everyone for the lively Q&A. Dropping a consolidated thread so we don't lose the follow-ups. Short and actionable.
Luis (Principal SWE): Two quick clarifications from the runtime roadmap: (1) kernel release rhythm? (2) batching defaults change?
Nia (Runtime PM): Kernel cadence: bi-weekly feature canaries, monthly larger rollouts. We'll start the first canary for the next kernel family in 5 days.
Kiran (ML Eng): For perf SLAs, can we commit to numbers per seq length bucket? Product wants clear thresholds for customer SLAs.
Maya (VP Eng): Yes. New SLA buckets: short (<=1k): p50<=25ms p95<=100ms, mid (1k-6k): p50<=70ms p95<=300ms, extended (6k-16k): p50<=180ms p95<=650ms. These apply to Hosted and Dedicated default configs.
Alex (SRE): Canary plan note: initial canary traffic 0.5%, run for 30m, if green expand to 5% for 2h. Console-bot will annotate traces with canary=true.
Console-bot: Canary scheduled: id=canary-212346, start=2026-04-12T20:00:00Z, initial_traffic=0.5%.
Luis (Principal SWE): Batching: we'll bump default dynamic_batch_token_limit from 10 -> 14 for text-gen and apply a lower default for long-context models. Flag name: `dynamic_batch_token_limit`.
Kiran (ML Eng): Will changing batch targets increase cold-start latency for long-context sessions? Need plan to isolate long-context cold requests.
Luis (Principal SWE): We'll route long-context cold-start requests to a low-batch lane (max batch tokens=4) to avoid tail latency spikes. Cache-aware routing will prefer cache-hit traffic for high-batch lanes.
Nia (Runtime PM): Cache TTL defaults: ephemeral prefixes=8m, session-affine=45m, user-session sticky=2h. We'll publish config matrix and recommended values in the docs.
Kiran (ML Eng): Nice. On quantization: customers ask if they should prefer 4-bit for real-time chat. Any guidance?
Maya (VP Eng): Action item: Kiran + Luis to assemble an internal note "quantization playbook" with measured regressions on quality and end-to-end latency for representative prompts. Due Tue EOD.
Alex (SRE): Canary rollback criteria proposal: any increase in p95 >7% over baseline OR new OOMs OR error-rate delta >4% sustained for 3 consecutive 1m samples triggers auto-rollback. Also alert paging on primary oncall.
Luis (Principal SWE): We'll add a lightweight smoke test in the canary that runs 150 character-limited prompts and 50 long-context prompts to check perf and mem. If smoke fails -> no expansion.
Nia (Runtime PM): Console UX: add small persistent banner during kernel canaries: "Runtime canary in progress 1 - minimal user impact expected" and include link to release notes.
Console-bot: UI ticket created: ui-3456, assignee=Console Team, due=2026-04-10.
Maya (VP Eng): One more thing: region/fallback routing. Default: local region preferred; if capacity low, route to nearest region within latency budget (configurable per tenant). We'll document the policy and expose tenant opt-out.
Kiran (ML Eng): Will kernel_variant be visible in traces? Helpful for debugging customer reports.
Luis (Principal SWE): Yes, we'll tag traces/logs with `kernel_variant` and `batching_profile`. Not returned in API payloads.
Alex (SRE): Ops note: new kernel uses different CUDA mem alloc pattern; we'll coordinate node draining earlier in the window to reduce pressure. Ops bot will post drain commands 15m before canary start.
Maya (VP Eng): Summary / action owners: (1) Kiran+Luis: quantization playbook (Tue EOD), (2) Luis: PR for `dynamic_batch_token_limit` + defaults (next week), (3) Alex: codify canary rollback rules + ops playbook (PR by Mon), (4) Console: canary banner (UI ticket ui-3456). I'll create calendar invites with check-ins.
Luis (Principal SWE): I'll open the batching PR and link it here when ready.
Kiran (ML Eng): I'll start the perf runs and share a short table of p50/p95 for the sample prompts.
Alex (SRE): I'll post the ops-runbook and drain schedule once synced with infra.
Maya (VP Eng): Thanks! If anyone else needs to follow up, drop it here. We'll keep this thread as the single source for action tracking. :white_check_mark:
